metas.name: Agriculture - Corn
metas.note: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Agriculture - Mendoza Vineyards
metas.note: If you see vineyards with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sorghum
metas.note: Fields of sorghum can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, Córdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.note: Fields of sunflowers are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.

metas.name: Agriculture - Tree Plantations
metas.note: The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

metas.name: Architecture - Mar del Plata Architecture
metas.note: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

metas.name: Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.note: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

metas.name: Car Meta - Sawdust Car Meta
metas.note: The “sawdust” car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Low Quality Sunset Coverage
metas.note: Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with Neuquén.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Melted Snow Coverage
metas.note: Melting snow coverage is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Snow Coverage
metas.note: This snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Sunrise Coverage with Blurs
metas.note: Sunrise coverage with bad image quality and multiple blurs is found on a short part of the RN251 and RN22, west of Río Colorado.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bariloche Taxi
metas.note: This taxi with the white body, blue roof and blue logo is unique to the city of Bariloche.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Buenos Aires Taxi
metas.note: This taxi with a black body and yellow roof is common in Buenos Aires. Note that taxis from Jujuy and Rosarío have the same combination. However, Buenos Aires is the only city where the taxi has the middle bar (behind the driver) painted.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Comodoro Rivadavia Taxi
metas.note: This all white taxi with a black logo is unique to Comodoro Rivadavia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cordoba km-marker
metas.note: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cordoba Taxi
metas.note: These all green or all yellow taxis with an oval shape beneath the driver door are unique to Cordoba.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Jujuy Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Jujuy have a black body and a yellow roof. Notably, only the top of the roof is yellow, making it distinct from Rosario or Buenos Aires taxis.

metas.name: Infrastructure - km-marker
metas.note: Argentinian kilometer markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top. RN stands for ruta national (white on the map), RP stands for ruta provincial (green on the map).

metas.name: Infrastructure - La Pampa Junction Sign
metas.note: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

metas.name: Infrastructure - La Plata Taxi
metas.note: La Plata has white taxis with green elements.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Latvian-style Poles
metas.note: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Mendoza Taxi
metas.note: This black and yellow taxi is unique to Mendoza. Jujuy, Rosario and Buenos Aires also have black and yellow taxis, but on those taxis, the body is completely black.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Neuquen Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Neuquen are all yellow. What distinguishes them from Cordoba taxis is that their doors have no logos or paintings on them.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Resistencia Taxi
metas.note: Taxis with a red-white-green stripe (hungarian flag) are unique to Resistencia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rosario Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Rosario have a black body and a yellow roof. The outer bars are yellow, while the middle bar (behind the driver) is black. This makes them distinguishable from taxis in Jujuy and Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Salta Taxi
metas.note: Red taxis with a black stripe are unique to Salta.

metas.name: Infrastructure - San Juan Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with a yellow roof are unique to San Juan.

metas.name: Infrastructure - San Luis Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with two light-blue stripes (resembling the Argentinian flag) are unique to San Luis.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Santiago del Estero Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with light-green roofs are unique to Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Single Hook Insulator
metas.note: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tucuman Pole ID
metas.note: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tucuman Taxi
metas.note: These old-school, white taxis with a yellow-black checkerboard stripe are unique to Tucuman.

metas.name: Landscape - Bahia Blanca Hills
metas.note: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.

metas.name: Landscape - Chaco & Formosa Landscape
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

metas.name: Landscape - Chenque Hill
metas.note: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

metas.name: Landscape - Cordoba Mountains
metas.note: These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.

metas.name: Landscape - Flat & Barren Landscape
metas.note: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

metas.name: Landscape - Grassland
metas.note: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

metas.name: Landscape - Mars Coverage
metas.note: The RP1 in Neuquen has dark, cloudy coverage. It is a dark red dirt road and thus resembles Mars. There is some spill onto the RP7 in the North and the RP10 in the South.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South Landscape
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Landscape - Mountains
metas.note: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Mountains
metas.note: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

metas.name: Landscape - Road of Death
metas.note: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Road of Death - Cloudy
metas.note: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.

metas.name: Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.note: Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

metas.name: Landscape - San Luis Roads
metas.note: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

metas.name: Landscape - Small Lakes and Ponds
metas.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Landscape - Talampaya National Park
metas.note: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.

metas.name: Landscape - Ushuaia
metas.note: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

metas.name: Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino
metas.note: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

metas.name: Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
metas.note: This unique dam with the rock formations typical for Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino can be found west of the town.

metas.name: Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

metas.name: Trekker - Horse Trekker
metas.note: This horse trekker can be found in southwestern San Juan.

metas.name: Vegetation - Azorella Prolifera - Light Green
metas.note:
Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia. It's appearence depends on season.

You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:

  • Southern Neuquen
  • Rio Negro on the roads Chasico-Laguna Blanca and Chasico-Ingeniero Jacobacci
  • Chubut in the area between Paso del Sapo and Gobernador Costa
  • Also Chubut on the National 40, south of Rio Mayo, as well as the provincial 55 branching east of the 40.
metas.footer: Source: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Beech Forest
metas.note: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.

metas.name: Vegetation - Butia Yatay Palm
metas.note: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caldén
metas.note: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caranday Palm
metas.note: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caranday Wax Palm
metas.note: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cardón
metas.note: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

metas.name: Vegetation - Macaw Palm
metas.note: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

metas.name: Vegetation - Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.note: The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on provincial road 23 + offroads, between Caviahue and Atreuco.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Pampas Grass
metas.note: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.note: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal and General Mosconi.

metas.name: Vegetation - Poplar Plantation - Mediterranean
metas.note:
Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.
metas.footer: Source: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Red Baron
metas.note:
Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue. It's found in

  • Western and Southern Santa Cruz
  • Northwestern Chubut
  • Southern Neuquen
metas.footer: Source: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Red Baron - Dense
metas.note:
Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.

In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:

  • Max South Santa Cruz, latitudes south of Rio Gallegos
  • The national 40 north of Las Horquetas (Santa Cruz)
  • The national 40 between Esquel and Estanzia Nueva Lubecka
metas.footer: Source: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Single Row Poplar - Flat
metas.note:
Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:

  • National 22 between Neuquen and Choele Choel (Rio Negro)
  • Trelew (Chubut)
  • Sarmiento (Chubut)
metas.footer: Source: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Vegetation - Toothpick Cactus
metas.note: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

metas.name: Vegetation - Wild Sunflower
metas.note: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
